question: A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with crushing substernal chest pain. The patient has a past medical history of obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. He drinks 5 alcoholic drinks every night and has a 40 pack-year smoking history. The patient works as a truck driver and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His initial electrocardiogram (ECG) is notable for ST elevation in V2-V5 with reciprocal changes. The patient is sent for cardiac catheterization, and several stents are placed. The patient is being monitored after the procedure, when he suddenly becomes less responsive. His temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 87/48 mmHg, pulse is 150/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Jugular venous distension is absent and pulmonary exam is notable for clear breath sounds bilaterally. The patient states that he is experiencing back and flank pain and is tender to palpation over his lumbar back and flanks. The patient is given 3 liters of Lactated Ringer solution and his blood pressure improves to 110/70 mmHg and his pulse is 95/min. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "ST elevation in V2-V5" -> "acute myocardial infarction" -> "cardiac catheterization and stenting" -> "sudden hypotension and tachycardia" -> "possible bleeding or vascular complication" -> "CT scan to evaluate for retroperitoneal bleed" -> 85%

CHAIN: "ST elevation in V2-V5" -> "acute myocardial infarction" -> "cardiac catheterization and stenting" -> "sudden hypotension and tachycardia" -> "back and flank pain" -> "possible retroperitoneal hemorrhage" -> "CT scan to confirm diagnosis" -> 90%

CHAIN: "ST elevation in V2-V5" -> "acute myocardial infarction" -> "cardiac catheterization and stenting" -> "sudden hypotension and tachycardia" -> "improved with fluids" -> "possible volume depletion or bleeding" -> "CT scan to assess for internal bleeding" -> 80%

CHAIN: "ST elevation in V2-V5" -> "acute myocardial infarction" -> "cardiac catheterization and stenting" -> "sudden hypotension and tachycardia" -> "clear lung sounds, no JVD" -> "unlikely heart failure or tamponade" -> "CT scan to rule out other causes" -> 75%

CHAIN: "ST elevation in V2-V5" -> "acute myocardial infarction" -> "cardiac catheterization and stenting" -> "sudden hypotension and tachycardia" -> "back and flank pain" -> "tenderness over lumbar and flanks" -> "possible retroperitoneal bleed" -> "CT scan to confirm" -> 85%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms suggestive of a retroperitoneal hemorrhage, a known complication following cardiac catheterization. The sudden onset of hypotension, tachycardia, and back/flank pain, along with the improvement in hemodynamics after fluid resuscitation, supports this diagnosis. A CT scan is the most appropriate next step to confirm the presence of a retroperitoneal bleed.
